## Overview

-   **Input:** `data/IMvigor210_plain.rds` (TPM and clinical tables;
    this file does not need script 01 to be run first)
-   **Output:** boxplots and a results table (medians, Wilcoxon
    p-values, BH-adjusted p-values and effect sizes) shown in the HTML
    report; no files are saved to `results/`.
-   **Comparison:** complete response (R, n = 25) vs progressive disease
    (NR, n = 167). TMB is missing for 42 patients.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
 
library(tidyverse)
```

### 1. Data Preparation and PDCD1 Expression

```{r}
#| label: data-preparation

IMvigor <- readRDS("../data/IMvigor210_plain.rds")

IMvigor_clinical <- IMvigor$clinical |>
  filter(BOR %in% c("R", "NR")) |>
  mutate(BOR = factor(BOR, levels = c("NR", "R")))

# Extract PDCD1 expression
PDCD1_tpm <- IMvigor$tpm |>
  data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column("ID") |> 
  filter(ID == "PDCD1") |> 
  select(-"ID") |> 
  unlist()

# Verify sample alignment
stopifnot(identical(IMvigor_clinical$sample_id, colnames(IMvigor$tpm)))

IMvigor_relevant <- IMvigor_clinical |> 
  mutate(PDCD1_TPM = PDCD1_tpm)
```

### 2. The Immune-related gene signature (GEP) (redone)

```{r}
#| label: gep-calculation

GEP_genes <- c(
  "CD27", "CD274", "PDCD1", "CD276", "CD8A", "CMKLR1",
  "CXCL9", "CXCR6", "HLA-DQA1", "HLA-DRB1", "HLA-E",
  "IDO1", "LAG3", "NKG7", "PDCD1LG2", "PSMB10", "STAT1", "TIGIT"
)

GEP_expr <- IMvigor$tpm |>
  data.frame() |> 
  rownames_to_column("ID") |> 
  filter(ID %in% GEP_genes) |> 
  column_to_rownames("ID") |> 
  as.matrix()

# Log-transform and standardize each gene across patients
GEP_expr_log <- log2(GEP_expr + 1)

GEP_expr_scaled <- t(scale(t(GEP_expr_log)))

# Calculate the mean standardized expression per patient
GEP_scores <- colMeans(GEP_expr_scaled)

stopifnot(identical(IMvigor_relevant$sample_id, names(GEP_scores)))

#Add to table
IMvigor_relevant <- IMvigor_relevant |> 
  mutate(ImmuneScoresGEP = GEP_scores)
```

### 3. Biomarker Distributions by Treatment Response

#### Tumor Mutational Burden (TMB)

```{r}
#| label: fig-tmb-distribution

IMvigor_relevant |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = BOR, y = TMB, color = BOR)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Best Overall Response",
    y = "Tumor Mutational Burden (mutations per megabase)",
    title = "Distribution of TMB in responses"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

#### PDCD1 Expression

```{r}
#| label: fig-pdcd1-distribution

IMvigor_relevant |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = BOR, y = log2(PDCD1_TPM + 1), color = BOR)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Best Overall Response",
    y = "log2(PDCD1_TPM +1)",
    title = "Distribution of PDCD1 in responses"
  )
```

#### Immune-related GEP Score

```{r}
#| label: fig-gep-distribution

IMvigor_relevant |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = BOR, y = ImmuneScoresGEP, color = BOR)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Best Overall Response",
    y = "ImmuneScoresGEP",
    title = "Distribution of GEP in responses"
  )
```

### 4. Statistical Comparison

Gene expression data can be skewed and contain zero values, while TMB is
often right-skewed. Therefore, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test was selected
to compare biomarker distributions between responders and non-responders
by ranking the data rather than comparing the values directly.

```{r}
#| label: wilcoxon-tests

# Compare biomarker distributions between response groups
# NA are automatically excluded
TMB_responseTest <- wilcox.test(TMB ~ BOR, data = IMvigor_relevant)
PD1_responseTest <- wilcox.test(PDCD1_TPM ~ BOR, data = IMvigor_relevant)
GEP_responseTest <- wilcox.test(ImmuneScoresGEP ~ BOR, data = IMvigor_relevant)
```

### 5. Summary of Statistical Results

```{r}
#| label: biomarker-results

#MAKE A TIBBLE THAT HAS THE DATA THAT WE CARE ABOUT
results <- tibble(
  Biomarker = c("TMB", "PDCD1", "GEP"),

  MedianR = c(
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R" & !is.na(IMvigor_relevant$TMB), ]$TMB),
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R", ]$PDCD1_TPM),
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R", ]$ImmuneScoresGEP)
  ),

  MedianNR = c(
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR" & !is.na(IMvigor_relevant$TMB), ]$TMB),
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR", ]$PDCD1_TPM),
    median(IMvigor_relevant[IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR", ]$ImmuneScoresGEP)
  ),

  n_R = c(
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R" & !is.na(IMvigor_relevant$TMB)),
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R"),
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "R")
  ),

  n_NR = c(
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR" & !is.na(IMvigor_relevant$TMB)),
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR"),
    sum(IMvigor_relevant$BOR == "NR")
  ),

  W = c(
    TMB_responseTest$statistic,
    PD1_responseTest$statistic,
    GEP_responseTest$statistic
  ),

  p_value = c(
    TMB_responseTest$p.value,
    PD1_responseTest$p.value,
    GEP_responseTest$p.value
  )
)
```

The table is now used to calculate additional parameters to better
explain the data and results.

```{r}
#| label: adjusted-results

results <- results |>
  mutate(
    p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significant = ifelse(p_adjusted < 0.05, yes = "YES", no = "NO"),
    MedianR = round(MedianR, 3),
    MedianNR = round(MedianNR, 3),
    EffectSize = 1 - (2 * W)/(n_R * n_NR) 
    #This is the Rank-biserial correlation and was used to calculate an effect size and compare the direction and magnitude
  )

results


```
